records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.296 scored 1/8. Seven of eight rollouts enumerated the candidates correctly and correctly derived that under one reading each speaker WOULD know the partner, then still reported a candidate they had just written was contradictory; the single success was the run that instead concluded that reading retains nothing and finished the other. The incumbent only states the deletion rule for 'not knowing' and never states its converse, so the student has no positive rule turning 'that speaker would know' into a kept-or-killed verdict and drifts back to an eliminated candidate. This edit adds that converse in five tokens and pays for it by dropping the 'do not reason from the original set' clause, which rounds 8 and 11 showed inert (identical held-out whether kept or removed), leaving the hint 9 tokens shorter than the incumbent with all load-bearing steps intact.

Fresh rollouts (148.297) scored 7/8. The single failure reached the correct x,y locus equation but its squared-term coefficient was not 1, so it looped ~49 times debating ellipse versus circle, even deriving the right center and radius then re-doubting, and hit the length cap without ever boxing an answer; it had also burned most of its budget parametrizing w by angle before finally inverting to a relation in z. Two incumbent clauses are inert here: 'geometrically' appeared in 1 of 8 traces and 'exceptional values' in 0 of 8. This revision spends those tokens on the two concrete moves the evidence demands - invert to |z-1|=R|z| immediately instead of parametrizing, and normalize the common squared-term coefficient - and is 68 tokens versus the incumbent's 70.

Rollouts scored 4/8. Every one of the eight write-ups after the reasoning block closed ignored the incumbent's box-first ordering: each restarted a full multi-step re-derivation and only reached the box 2000-2500 characters later. Two of the four failures were truncated mid-restart with no box at all, despite already holding the right value inside the reasoning. So the losing clause is inert as worded, while the underlying gate is real. This edit keeps box-first but makes it executable as a concrete length budget (at most three lines, box in the first) and attaches the consequence, which should transfer to any problem where a verbose recap eats the answer.

Five of eight rollouts (148.299) were correct; all three failures shared one mode: they never split the inputs into per-polynomial parts, so they imposed P(x)=A+Bx as an identity for all x, derived that a degree-5 polynomial must be constant or linear, and either answered the menu size or looped to the token limit. The correct ones all explicitly assigned each polynomial its own block of inputs first. This edit names that partition as an executable step before the degree count, restoring a grouping step the round-12 rewrite had dropped, and does so in 141 tokens versus the incumbent's 146.

5/8 correct; all three misses hit finish_reason=length with no boxed answer. Each pinned the constants and reached the right single-unknown equation, then treated finding the admissible root as the goal: they never converted it into the quantity actually requested, instead sliding into decimal probing (105 and 143 approximation signs in two misses versus 0-3 in every success) and testing sample values until the budget ran out. All five successes went straight from the root to the requested quantity. The incumbent's closing line says to box the candidate, which is what the failures did; retargeting it to the quantity the candidate yields keeps the same length while naming the missing final step, and it transfers to any problem where the solved unknown is a means, not the answer.

Fresh rollouts scored 1/8. The failure is one error repeated in all eight: every rollout wrote that the shed's bottom bag is the one delivered LAST, then priced that, giving 1/4 (five runs), 1/24, 1/16 or 1 - and eight of eight reached it via an equally-likely-permutation claim. The incumbent already states the correct fact adjacently (round 14's win) and forbids the uniform shortcut, so no new wording of either idea is untested here: rounds 12 and 13 already lost by editing that bottom fact, and rounds 2-5, 10, 11 lost by adding content. Clause grep shows labeling 7/8, stacks 8/8, push/pop 5/8, one-half 8/8 all in use, while sum-to-one and red-flag appear 0/8 yet rounds 6 and 7 lost held-out when those were cut. So this round changes no strategy: every content phrase stays byte-identical and only four redundant function words go, banking a 3-token tiebreak at zero transfer risk.

Fresh rollouts scored 1/8; seven produced no correct boxed value. The sole winner rebuilt the problem at sizes 3 and 4, eliminated, recorded the two values with signs and generalized. Five losers instead shrank the wrong thing or kept a mismatched equation ladder, hit a degenerate 0=1 case, declared 'contradiction / must be a mistake' and abandoned the table for Vandermonde theory to the 16k cap. One loser paraphrased the incumbent as 'the coefficients are set to 2, 3, 4', the same misreading logged in round 7: 'the huge parameter' never says WHICH quantity shrinks. So I rename only that target - rebuild the whole problem at size n, which scales unknowns and equations together - and keep the ratio clause and closing verbatim since replacing either lost held-out in rounds 7, 9, 10 and 13. The twin prohibitions are merged, a rewording round 11 measured held-out-neutral, so this stays no longer than the incumbent.

Fresh rollouts scored 6/8; all 8 reached the gcd and enumerated the divisor candidates, but zero of 8 ever used the incumbent's grouping clause or its substitute-numbers-last clause, so both are inert transfer tax. The two failures picked among surviving candidates by which one 'looked reasonable', and one even contradicted its own divisor list. The edit swaps the two ignored clauses for a concrete first move rollouts already half-do (write one total = count x per-item equation per given) plus an executable selection rule (evaluate every candidate, then decide with an as-yet-unused stated condition instead of plausibility). Same length as the incumbent, 123 tokens.

4 of 8 correct. Every winner carried the leftover parameter as a letter and let its coefficient vanish in the requested values; all three length-capped failures instead pinned it to a concrete number early, then drowned in fractional arithmetic and looped on "contradiction" (5-12 times each, 39-83 "Wait") with nothing boxed, and the one wrong finisher was the heaviest numeric guesser of all. Meanwhile the incumbent tail "rather than solving for every coefficient" appears in no trace and is contradicted by the winners, who do solve the reduced relations. Swapping that inert clause for the single discipline the successes share - keep the free parameter symbolic - is a positive move that transfers to any underdetermined family whose requested quantity is parameter-independent, at 146 tokens versus the incumbent 147.

5/8 correct. Both budget-death failures spent the entire completion arguing abstractly about structure - never writing a concrete case - and emitted no boxed answer; a third asserted a structure it had not written out and boxed the wrong value. The incumbent's core instruction only fires when the asked quantity is a return count, so on unseen problems asking for something else its central step is inert. This edit keeps the same procedure (settle the setup, work the smallest case literally, tabulate more sizes, fit and check one formula, box it) but retargets it at whatever quantity is asked and makes 'every row comes from a case you actually wrote out' the load-bearing rule, replacing the period-specific clause the rollouts never used. It is also 1 token shorter than the incumbent.
